messages:
Leah: Hey all — I’m Leah, started today! Quick bootstrap Q: on an M1 Mac, trying to get asdf + brew working for Python 3.11 and node 18. When I run `asdf install nodejs 18.17.1` I hit an openssl compile error. Anyone run this recently? Any short checklist I should follow?

sam: welcome Leah :tada: First, make sure Homebrew is the ARM one at /opt/homebrew. Then install dependencies: `brew install openssl@1.1 readline pkg-config gpg` (gpg needed for nodejs plugin). Add brew to your PATH in ~/.zprofile if not already.

jamie: also set env vars before building native deps: `export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib"` and `export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include"` and `export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib/pkgconfig"`. Put those in your shell profile so asdf build picks them up.

marta: our dotfiles repo has a bootstrap script that symlinks configs and adds the PATH bits: `git clone git@github.com:redwood/dotfiles.git && cd dotfiles && ./bootstrap.sh`. If you prefer, I can run it with you — ping me and we’ll screenshare.

Leah: thanks — small detail: the nodejs plugin asked me to import gpg keys and then `bash node-vm.sh` or something. Is that required? I tried `asdf plugin-add nodejs` and it failed the gpg step.

sam: yep you need the nodejs plugin's gpg key setup once: `bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring` (the plugin docs mention it). If gpg errors, install gpg with brew and retry.

jamie: if you still see compile failures after that, try installing prebuilt binaries by setting `NODE_BUILD_NODEJS_ORG_MIRROR=https://nodejs.org` in your env or use asdf install with `ASDF_NODEJS_USE_DIST=1` (we prefer compiling for reproducibility but dist is quicker for onboarding).

Leah: one more — SSH key + repo access flow? Should I add my key to GitHub now or wait for ops?

infra-bot: created onboarding ticket #ONB-482 for Leah. Please add your public key to GitHub; infra will grant repo access once key is visible. Also join the 1:1 access queue if you need special perms.

sam: quick SSH: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "leah@redwood.ai"` then `pbcopy < ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` and paste in GitHub > Settings > SSH Keys. After that, DM me and I’ll run the access request.

marta: dotfiles note — our bootstrap will optionally create a `.env.local` stub for local secrets; do NOT commit real secrets. We use 1Password + repo secrets for anything shared.

Leah: awesome, this is super helpful. I’ll try these steps and DM if stuck. Thanks everyone! :heart:

marta: happy to pair later today if you want — I’ve added you to the dotfiles PR review team. :+1:
